items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1979-12-05
items.q: Lee Collins, that's when I recorded that thing they called it, Astoria Hot 8. We had Sid Averdino clan... That's what we call that the old Italian Hall. That's the first recording I ever made.

ctx.x: And you were playing banjo at this time?

At that time I was born for the Stikker Steamboat Company. Uh-huh. And there was a ten piece band. It had three sax, three brass, and four rhythms. And you had to play banjo, you had to play pangeline guitar. If you were bass, you had to play bass following and bass horn. I worked with, I started with Fate Marble, and then they had a job with Sidney Desveen, and that's where he came to me. We used to play at the country club on Sundays. And that's where the Captain Vaughan came in and heard the band and I used to…
Yeah, for about ten years. And that's when you.

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1961-01-29
items.q: Lee Collin had that job, too, you see, and I didn't want that

ctx.x: Picked him up, that's why he was actually on the session. Yeah. So it wasn't Albert Martin on the session? No,

no, no. He, he, he was already out of town in Texas. Yeah. So, um, when they tell him it come time for the boat to leave, well, I had told him to put my notice in it, and I had recommended, which they all liked it, Danny Barker. Yeah. That's how Danny Barker got in there. That was right after the recording, was it? Yeah, shortly after the recording, yeah. Mm-hmm. And, um, I don't know, on the record, they used Rennie Hall, but I don't know, Rennie might have played, like, when I have, when I was out of town after…
because I was satisfied going on the boat. But it was you on all, all, all the records then? Oh, yeah,
